newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey tenders for plant to sell water to Mideast.
newsitem.headline: Turkey tenders for plant to sell water to Mideast.

text.p: Turkey invited an international tender on Wednesday for a project to rent a fresh water purification and treatment plant in its south for water sales to Middle Eastern countries, state hydraulics authority (DSI) said.

The project, announced through the tender in the Official Gazette, envisages that the operator will first complete unfinished construction work, started in 1992 by the government but left off due to financial problems.
It will later operate the plant, to be on the Manavgat river near Antalya on the Mediterranean, and market fresh water, to be produced at a daily rate of 500,000 cubic metres.
The project is part of the government's revenue raising packages and is expected to earn the government 120 trillion lira ($1 billion) over the 20 years of leasing life.
The companies should hand in their bids by February 14 to the head office of DSI in Ankara.
DSI General Manager Dogan Altinbilek said the construction work could be completed in one year.
"The operator company will pay royalties to the government for each cubic metre of water it sells," he said.
Officials earlier said they expect countries around the Mediterranean, especially Israel, Libya, Malta and Italy, to show interest in the project.
The operator company will build a 10-km (six-mile) twin pipeline to carry water from the plant to a loading port.
Accoring to the tender terms, bidders, either individual companies or consortia, should have a minimum $10 million annual turnover and submit letters of guarantee worth at least $5 million.

Officials said per tonne production cost of Manavgat water would be up to $3, compared to $6 for water produced through desalination of sea water, a method used by many Mediterranean and Middle East countries.
DSI officials said some of the water to be produced could be transported to Turkey's tourist attractions of Kemer, Bordum and Belek, where water supply is a serious problem during long summers.
